# oc-ctx-handover

An OpenCode plugin that replaces automatic context compaction with a **deliberate handover**: when a session approaches its context limit, the agent is stopped and made to write a handover document (`HANDOVER.md`) describing what it did, what is unfinished, and what to do next. Depending on how the handover was started, the same session is compacted and continues from the document, or the session is left as it is and the next session in that directory starts from it.

## Handover vs. regular compaction

Regular compaction waits until the context is nearly full, then asks the model for an automatic summary of the transcript and continues from that summary. It replaces the session's history with a lossy, machine-generated digest of everything — including all the dead ends — and you have no say in what it keeps.

This plugin moves the decision earlier and hands the instructions on how to continue to the agent:

| | Regular compaction | oc-ctx-handover |
| --- | --- | --- |
| When | near the context limit | at 80% of the limit (configurable), or on demand via `/handover` |
| Who writes the summary | the model, as an extra summarization call | the agent itself, as a document you can read and edit |
| What survives | whatever the summarizer judged important | the current step, decisions made, next steps — and anything you name in `/handover <note>` |
| Cost | an extra model call to produce the summary | no extra context read at handover time: the model already knows what it needs to write |
| Afterwards | the session continues from a summary you never see | the same session continues from `HANDOVER.md` (with `--continue`), or the next session in that directory starts from it (`/handover`) |

The session id never changes: the compaction happens in place, so the TUI keeps its focus and no empty session is left behind. `/handover` does not compact at all — it writes the document and leaves the session alone.

## Install

Published on npmjs as `@troed/oc-ctx-handover`. There is no build step and no dependencies — OpenCode loads the shipped TypeScript directly through the package-root `index.ts`.

```sh
opencode plugin add @troed/oc-ctx-handover@latest
```

That adds the package to `plugins` in your global OpenCode config (`~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`). Pin a version by replacing `@latest` with it, for example `@troed/oc-ctx-handover@0.1.0`; an unpinned entry is checked for updates without changing the installed package.

To configure the plugin in the config file instead of the environment, use the object form with `options` (see [Configuration](#configuration)):

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@troed/oc-ctx-handover",
      "options": { "threshold": 0.8 }
    }
  ]
}
```

To enable the plugin for a single project, put the same entry in that project's `opencode.jsonc` or `.opencode/opencode.jsonc` instead of the global config.

Then load it:

```sh
opencode service restart
```

Verify it registered by checking its log:

```sh
tail -n 20 ~/.local/share/opencode/log/oc-ctx-handover.log
```

On a working install the log ends with lines like:

```
[oc-ctx-handover] ... session api: compact=ok prompt=ok context=ok get=ok
[oc-ctx-handover] ... compaction hook registered
[oc-ctx-handover] ... handover command registered
[oc-ctx-handover] ... context hook registered
```

The file is created by the plugin itself, so it will not exist until the plugin has run at least once.

That's it. Sessions now hand over at 80% of the model's context limit. `HANDOVER.md` is written to the session's project directory; add it to your `.gitignore` unless you want it committed.

The plugin needs OpenCode V2 (`ctx.session.hook`, `ctx.session.compact`, `ctx.command.transform`). The startup read uses `ctx.session.context` and, when the build exposes it, `ctx.session.get`. On a build without them it logs why and stays out of the way.

### From a checkout (development)

```sh
git clone <this-repo> <local path>/oc-ctx-handover
```

Add the **directory** to `plugins`:

```jsonc
{
  "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json",
  "plugins": [
    "<local path>/oc-ctx-handover"
  ]
}
```

Point at the directory containing `index.ts`, not at a file. Relative paths (`./plugins/oc-ctx-handover`) resolve against the config file. To enable it for a single project only, drop the directory in `<project>/.opencode/plugins/oc-ctx-handover/` instead — plugins there load automatically. The object form above works with the directory path in place of the package name, and a running service picks up edits on reload.

## Usage

Automatic: nothing to do. When a step would start within 4,096 tokens of the 80% ceiling, or usage reaches the ceiling, the agent is told to stop and write the document.

The document step is capped at a **document budget** — 5% of the model's context limit, bounded to 4,096–32,768 tokens — and the instruction names that budget, so the model can size the document instead of being cut off mid-write. The only tool the instruction allows is the one that writes the file. While the document is missing the instruction is re-sent on each step (the host may add its own prompt in between, e.g. a goal continuation, and hook-appended messages are not stored in the session history), up to three instructions. If the document still is not written, or if less than 2,048 tokens remain before the hard limit, no document can fit: the plugin stops the step and queues a regular compaction (once per session) instead of dispatching a doomed write.

On demand: type the command at any context level.

```
/handover
/handover capture the migration plan and the two failing tests
/handover --continue
/handover --continue finish the auth refactor before anything else
```

`/handover` **leaves** the session. The agent stops, writes `HANDOVER.md`, and nothing else happens: no compaction, no continue prompt, no new session. Close the session whenever you like; the next session in that directory picks the document up (see [Starting from a document](#starting-from-a-document)).

`/handover --continue` is the in-place handover the threshold performs: the agent writes the document, the session is compacted, and the fresh context is told to continue from it. The session id does not change.

In both forms the optional note after the command becomes a requirement for the document.

## Starting from a document

When a session starts with no history in a directory that already has a `HANDOVER.md`, the plugin appends an instruction to the system prompt: read the document first, continue that work if the request is about it, and follow the user's request otherwise. The document is never edited or deleted by the plugin — it stays a working document the agent can keep up to date for the rest of the session.

Two guards keep an old document from claiming a new session: one last written more than `readMaxAgeDays` days ago is left on disk but not offered (the work it describes is probably finished), and a subagent's child session is never offered it.

## Configuration

Settings come from the plugin `options` in `opencode.jsonc` (object form) or, when the plugin is registered as a bare string, from the environment of the OpenCode service at plugin load. A value set in `options` takes precedence over the matching environment variable; an unset or unusable value falls back to the default rather than failing, and the plugin never throws into a session.

```jsonc
{
  "plugins": [
    {
      "package": "@troed/oc-ctx-handover",
      "options": {
        "threshold": 0.8,
        "thresholds": { "providerID/modelID": 0.6 }
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

| Option | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `threshold` | `0.8` | Fraction of the model's context limit at which the handover fires (`0`-`1`). |
| `thresholds` | `{}` | Per-model overrides keyed by `providerID/modelID`, each a fraction in `0`-`1`. A model with no entry uses `threshold`. |
| `readMaxAgeDays` | `14` | How old (in days) an existing handover document may be for a new session to be pointed at it. Must be positive. |

Environment equivalents (used when `options` does not set them):

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `OC_CTX_HANDOVER_THRESHOLD` | `0.8` | Fraction of the model's context limit at which the handover fires (`0`–`1`). |
| `OC_CTX_HANDOVER_HANDOFF_FILE` | `HANDOVER.md` | Where the document goes. A relative path resolves against the session's project directory; an absolute path is used as-is. |
| `OC_CTX_HANDOVER_READ_MAX_AGE_DAYS` | `14` | How old (in days) an existing document may be for a new session to be pointed at it. |
| `OC_CTX_HANDOVER_LOG_FILE` | `~/.local/share/opencode/log/oc-ctx-handover.log` | Diagnostics log. |
| `OC_CTX_HANDOVER_DISABLED` | unset | `1`, `true` or `yes` disables the plugin. |

An unset or unusable value falls back to the default rather than failing; the plugin never throws into a session.

## Troubleshooting

Every step logs one usage line, so the log is the first place to look:

```
usage 132000/200000 tokens (66.0%) [measured] anchor=131000, threshold 80%, session ses_..., model provider/model
```

- **`[measured]` vs `[estimated]`** — `measured` means the provider-reported token count was available and only the growth since it was estimated. `estimated` means the whole payload was estimated from characters; the plugin still works, just less precisely.
- **Nothing in the log** — the plugin is not loaded: check that `plugins` contains the package name (or, for a checkout, the directory rather than a file), then restart the service and look in `~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log` for load errors.
- **`disabled: set OC_CTX_HANDOVER_DISABLED=0`** — the kill switch is set to a truthy value; unset it.
- **`no ctx.session.hook on this build`** — the OpenCode build is too old (pre-V2); the plugin registers nothing.
- **`no ctx.command.transform on this build; /handover is not registered`** — the threshold handover still works, only the command is missing.
- **A new session is not told to read `HANDOVER.md`** — the log line `starts with the existing handover document` is the positive case. If it is absent, the document is older than `readMaxAgeDays`, the session already has history, the session is a subagent's child, or the build does not report a session context at all.

## Development

```sh
node --test                       # test suite (node:test)
npx -p typescript tsc --noEmit    # typecheck (fetches TypeScript; none is vendored)
```

`index.ts` is the OpenCode entrypoint and only re-exports `src/index.ts`, so the directory OpenCode loads is the directory you edit — a running service picks up changes on reload.
